editorial_contributions.text: The paper characterizes the generalized dualities by showing that these dualities are determined by forbidding homomorphisms from a finite set of forests. In particular, it is shown that, up to homomorphic equivalence, if (\(F, D\)) is a generalized duality, then \(F\) is a set of forests and \(D\) is uniquely determined by \(F\). It also provides the construction of \(D\) from any finite set of forests \(F\). Furthermore, \(F\) is also uniquely determined by a possible right-hand side \(D\). As a result, the paper demonstrates that the decision problem, whether for a finite set \(H\) of graphs, there exists \(F\) such that (\(F, H\)) is a generalized duality, is NP-complete.

title.title: On sparse graphs with given colorings and homomorphisms.

editorial_contributions.text: Suppose that \(G=(V,E)\) is a graph and \(k,d\) are positive integers with \(k\geq 2d\) and \((k,d)=1\). A \((k,d)\)-coloring of \(G\) is a mapping \(f:V\rightarrow \{0,1,\ldots, k-1\}\) such that for every edge \(xy\in E\), min\(\{|f(x)-f(y)|, k-|f(x)-f(y)|\}\geq d\). In this paper the following property is constructively proved: If \(k\geq 3d-2, (k,d)=1\), \(A\) is a finite set and \(f_{1},\ldots ,f_{n}\) are mappings from \(A\) to \(\{0,1,\ldots ,k-1\}\), then for any integer \(l\), there is a graph \(G=(V,E)\) of girth at least \(l\) with \(A\subset V\), such that \(G\) has exactly \(n\) \((k,d)\)-colorings \(g_1,\dots, g_n\) (up to a permutation of the colors), and each \(g_{i}\) is an extension of \(f_{i}\). This result generalizes a result of \textit{V. Müller} who proved this for \(k\)-colorings [Discrete Math. 26, No. 2, 165-176 (1979; Zbl 0407.05037)]. Note that for \(n=1\), the method presented in this paper gives a construction of uniquely \((k,d)\)-colorable graphs. Some other results about the projectivity of the graphs \(G_{d}^{k}\) defined in the paper are also presented.

editorial_contributions.text:
[For the entire collection see Zbl 0548.00012.] 


Let \(H=(V,E)\) be a p-uniform hypergraph on \(| V| =n\) vertices. A strong k-colouring of H is a partition of V into k classes such that the vertices of any hyperedge of E belong to mutually different classes. H is said to be uniquely k-colourable if H has a k-colouring and the partition is uniquely determined. Let \(f^ k_ p(n)\) denote the minimal size of E of uniquely k-colourable p-uniform hypergraphs on n vertices. Upper and lower bounds for \(f^ k_ p(n)\) are presented, which imply e.g. 
\[
 n- 2\leq f^ 4_ 3(n)\leq n-1,\quad (2(k-1)/(p^ 2-p))n\leq \lim_{n\to \infty}f^ k_ p(n)\leq (2(2k-p)/p^ 2)n. 
\]
 The special cases \(k=p\) and \(p=2\) were studied more in detail by the authors separately.

title.title: Minimal test sets for unique colourablity

editorial_contributions.text:
[For the entire collection see Zbl 0709.00011.]


Let \(H=(V,E)\) be a \(p\)-uniform hypergraph, i.e. \(V=\{x_ 1,\dots,x_ n\}\), \(E=\{M_ 1,\dots,M_ s\}\subseteq 2^ V\), \(| M_ i|=p\), \(i=1,\dots,s\). A strong colouring \(c\) of \(H\) is a function \(c:V\to\mathbb{N}\) with \(c(v)\neq c(v')\), if there is an edge \(M\in E\) with \(\{v,v'\}\subseteq M\). \(f^ p_ k(n)\) is defined to be the minimal number of hyperedges of a \(p\)-uniform hypergraph \(H\) which has \(n\) vertices and is uniquely \(k\)-colourable. \(f_ k(n)=f^ k_ k(n)\) for all integers \(n\geq 2\), \(k\geq 2\). The authors present results on lower and upper bound of \(f_ k(n)\).

editorial_contributions.text: Results on Ramsey matroids together with some open problems are summarized. Using the method of matroid amalgamation, the following theorem is proved. Let M be a matroid and G be a subgroup of its automorphism group Aut M. Then there exists a matroid N such that (i) M is a restriction of N, (ii) Aut N is isomorphic to G, (iii) every automorphism of G extends uniquely to an automorphism of N.
